title: Requirements skill
summary: Produce a traceable brief with supported behavior and open questions.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.text: The request, reviewed decisions, relevant source material, affected implementation versions where available and existing acceptance evidence.

sections.label: Procedure
sections.text: Establish intended behavior; classify evidence and uncertainty; trace affected components; derive acceptance scenarios; identify missing decisions.

sections.label: Output
sections.text: A brief with scope, sources, requirement status, dependencies, scenarios, owner, and unresolved questions.

sections.label: Failure condition
sections.text: Missing authority or conflicting requirements must remain unresolved; the skill must not invent a decision.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Use the existing Requirements and evidence connection to write a brief that links intended behavior and verification to the actual source authority. The workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Only the source contribution below was verified on 15 October 2026, not every original assertion or project outcome.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: Each material requirement has a stable identifier, source location, scope, owner and explicit status.
The brief connects requirements to checkable examples and names the proposed verification evidence.
Conflicting or missing authority remains unresolved with an owner and next decision, rather than becoming an invented requirement.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: NASA Appendix D recommends a verification matrix that uniquely identifies each shall requirement included in the matrix, records its source document and defines how it is verified. This source supports traceability and verification planning. The Atlas brief structure is an adaptation and does not impose NASA policy or establish the truth of project requirements. Review date: 15 October 2026. This review covers this source contribution only, not the whole guide.

catalog.applicability: Use when a request needs a traceable brief that states the intended behavior, its sources, acceptance scenarios and the decisions still missing. Missing authority or conflicting requirements stay unresolved, the skill does not invent a decision.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.

claims.text: NASA Appendix D recommends a verification matrix that uniquely identifies each shall requirement included in the matrix, records its source document and defines how it is verified.
